next_step: Run cost-optimization workshop week of 2025-02-22; start Dedicated POC after workshop; internal finance approval by 2025-03-05
notes:
Account summary:
- Mid-market product org building an in-app assistant + semantic search for knowledge base and user personalization.
- Current prototype uses hosted API for quick iteration; primary ask is predictable unit economics as usage grows.
- Interested in Hosted -> Dedicated runway: start hosted for rapid rollout, move to Dedicated for steady throughput and cost predictability.

Technical & business requirements (short):
- Workloads: chat assistant (low-latency, conversational state), embeddings for search (high throughput), reranking for personalization.
- Latency targets: 95p < 250ms for assistant baseline; best-effort for embeddings throughput > 200 reqs/s during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: high for embeddings at scale (freemium users + nightly reindex). Target reducing per-embed cost by >= 60%.
- Model preferences: open Llama-family & quantized variants; willing to test 4-bit/8-bit quantized builds if quality acceptable.
- Routing/fallback: want auto-fallback to cheaper model for non-critical routes; region-aware routing for EU users.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, retention and residency policies for EU data.

Evaluation history & POC notes:
- 2025-01-15 discovery call (Maya, Ravi + product lead Sarah K): initial fit. Fireflies ff_2025-01-15_9253.
- 2025-01-21 quick hosted sandbox kickoff: onboarded product team, ran smoke tests. Observed ~2.4ms token generation on hosted benchmark (non-contended).
- 2025-01-28 demo: end-to-end assistant flow with conversation memory. Customer asked: "Can this scale without surprise bills?"
- 2025-02-04 cost deep-dive call with Redwood Optimize team (ff_2025-02-04_1129). Covered batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization tradeoffs.
- 2025-02-11 internal data share: they provided sample traffic histogram and prompt length distributions (drive://slatebridge/traffic-sample.csv).
- 2025-02-14 hosted API pilot results: baseline hosted cost estimate = ~$0.28 per 1k chat tokens; embeddings at ~$0.20 per 1k embed units (rough). Customer flagged embeddings as largest spend.

Cost-optimization workshop (planned outcomes):
- Workshop goals: 1) quantify unit-economics per route; 2) propose batching and caching config to hit target per-embed cost; 3) recommend quantization profile(s) and quality guardrails; 4) map Dedicated node sizing and expected monthly commit.
- Suggested workshop agenda: traffic analysis -> batching/caching simulation -> quantization A/B plan -> Dedicated sizing & pricing model -> procurement readiness checklist.
- Early recommendations from SE (Ravi): enable KV prefix caching for common help queries (expected 25-40% token reduction), configure dynamic batching for embeddings with batch size 64-256 depending on latency SLO, test int8 and nf4 quantization on local replica to validate MRR quality delta.
- Preliminary unit economics modeled in-drive: expected embedding cost reduction 60-75% on Dedicated + batching/caching + quantization. See drive://slatebridge/eo_model_v1.xlsx (stub).

Quotes & customer sentiment:
- Product lead Sarah K: "We need a clear path from prototype to a predictable ops model — engineering can't handle surprises on billing."
- CTO Alan R: "If Dedicated gives 3x cost savings on embeddings with similar quality, we can justify the commit."

Next steps (actionable):
- Schedule 2-3hr cost-optimization workshop with Redwood Optimize + SEs (owner: Maya) — target week of 2025-02-22.
- Prep: customer to provide 7-day traffic trace + sample prompts (done), Redwood to run batching/caching sim and return a summary 48h before workshop.
- Post-workshop: 2-week Dedicated POC (limited capacity, production-like traffic replay), cost & quality report, contract term sheet draft.

Blockers & risks:
- Legal: data residency clause needs redline; currently under review by SlateBridge counsel.
- Finance: internal procurement wants clear ARR impact and break-even timeline.
- Technical: need validation that 4-bit quantization maintains acceptable reranking AUC — will run evals during POC.
